title: B134 — CPU request management: right-size reservations + move more systems on-demand
description:
## ↑ HIGH 2026-09-26 — the cost/benefit gate has flipped

The 09-19 hold reasoned that only B44 (Medium) needed mother memory, so building a sleep platform for one marginal tool was disproportionate. Now it blocks two High items: **B159** ([EMA-216](https://linear.app/emangini/issue/EMA-216/b159-onboarding-services-represent-the-onboarding-flow-as-real), onboarding services) and **B161** ([EMA-218](https://linear.app/emangini/issue/EMA-218/b161-investigate-and-implement-dify), Dify Phase 2). It also gates B44, B76 and the ReportPortal candidate in B189. Mother memory is the lab's ranking bottleneck, so B134 moves up to match what it blocks.

## Hardware candidate (2026-09-26, not yet bought — likely)

A **Ryzen AI Max+ 395 ("Strix Halo")** box: 16C/32T Zen 5 + Radeon 8060S iGPU (40 CU, RDNA 3.5, gfx1151) sharing ONE pool of soldered LPDDR5X (64/96/128 GB; no upgrade later). Planned as **Proxmox**, mirroring Weyland's layout:

| On the new box | Runs | Why |
| -- | -- | -- |
| k3s worker VM | joins mother's cluster as a 2nd node | the CPU + RAM this item needs |
| Inference LXC (the CT 102 pattern) | Ollama/llama.cpp on Vulkan, `/dev/dri` + `/dev/kfd` bound in | the GPU; Bifrost/LiteLLM route to it as one more provider |

* **Buy the 128 GB model.** VM, LXC and GPU share one fixed pool; \~48 GB to the k3s VM + the rest to inference (a 70B-class model fits) adds \~2/3 of mother's RAM. 64 GB forces RAM *or* GPU.
* **GPU in an LXC, not the VM** — iGPU passthrough to a VM is unreliable; an LXC shares the host's `amdgpu`, like CT 102.
* **GPU software (checked 2026-09-26):** Vulkan is the reliable Linux path for gfx1151; ROCm still maturing (AMD targets ROCm 8.0); vLLM runs with effort. Does NOT replace rogueone — training, `rag-embed`, B111 vLLM/SGLang stay on CUDA.
* **No 2-node Proxmox cluster** (loses quorum when either box is down) — two standalone hosts or a QDevice; Kubernetes spans the machines.
* **Networking:** MS-A2 has 10GbE; Strix Halo boxes vary 2.5–10GbE; pods reach MinIO/Postgres on mother over it — prefer 10GbE.
* **What moves:** stateless workloads first; stateful stores, their local-path PVs and the backups stay pinned to mother (docs/dr.md blast radius unchanged). The join brings node labels + pinning and a pass over single-node assumptions (schedules.md Rule #4, hostPath backups).
* Unblocks on landing: B159, B161 Phase 2, B44, **B200** ([EMA-286](https://linear.app/emangini/issue/EMA-286/b200-parallel-ci-across-more-build-agents-on-new-hardware) — parallel CI on more build agents). Purchase is the owner's call.
* **Storage: 4 TB is plenty.** Today mother's root disk uses 685 / 1,178 GiB and MinIO 580 GiB of 3.9 TiB (17%). The box needs \~300–600 GB for models (70B Q4 ≈ 40 GB) + \~100–200 GB for node images.
* **DR bonus — a stated goal of the purchase:** the spare space holds a full MinIO copy, putting backups on a second machine for the first time. Closes two docs/dr.md gaps (core Postgres dumps and `rogueone-backup` exist only on mother's USB). Same house, so not off-site. Add dr.md rows when it lands.
* **vLLM / SGLang (checked 2026-09-26): possible, experimental.** Neither lists gfx1151 as supported. vLLM needs a ROCm-nightly build and `--enforce-eager` (HIP-graph stability bug) and decodes below llama.cpp on the same box; SGLang runs from community images (a `gfx1151` build dated 2026-09-23). \~256 GB/s bandwidth caps single-stream speed; vLLM/SGLang pay off under concurrency. **Default serving = Ollama/llama.cpp on Vulkan;** vLLM/SGLang here are B111-style experiments — the CUDA path on rogueone stays primary.

## RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 — the premise changed, and item 4 is now answered

**The CPU wall dissolved on its own.** Requests went **17.34 -> 12.97 cores** over the week; the step change is 08-22, the KEDA retirement (10 pods). Today: **12,970m requested (81%) against 2,764m used (17%)**, zero Pending pods, zero `FailedScheduling` events. CPU trimming now buys future headroom, not relief.

**Memory is the binding constraint, and unlike CPU it is honest.**

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Memory requested | 66.7 Gi (92%) |
| **7d peak concurrent usage** | **67.4 Gi** |
| Allocatable | 72.0 Gi |
| Headroom at peak | **4.6 Gi** |

### Item 4 is answered with data: requests CANNOT be honest on this node

Setting every request to its measured per-pod p95 totals **96.8 Gi on a 72 Gi node (134%)**. That is not a policy choice - requests must sum under allocatable, honest per-pod reservations sum to \~97 Gi, so the contract is unsatisfiable. The cluster works today only because requests are *collectively understated* while peaks do not coincide.

So "make the scheduler honest" is unachievable by construction on a single node. Per-pod accuracy and a single-node ceiling are incompatible. **Sum of per-pod percentiles (96.8) is not the percentile of the sum (67.4)** - the second is the number that OOMs the node.

### DONE — surgical right-sizing (net -768 Mi, verified live)

| Pod | Request | Limit | Basis |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `trino` | 3 -> **5.5 Gi** | 8 Gi | p50 4.91 / p95 6.80. **OOMKilled 2026-08-23, 16 restarts** - the only pod with a demonstrated failure from under-reservation |
| `dagster-user-code` | 4 -> **1.75 Gi** | 12 Gi | p50 0.91 / p95 1.40. Had request and limit confused: a 4 Gi floor held all day to protect a 02:17 burst the 12 Gi limit already covers |
| `llama-guard` | 2 -> **1 Gi** | 4 Gi | p50 0.20 / p95 0.62 |

Verified: all three Running, `up{job="trino"}`=1, `/metrics` HTTP 200, node memory requests 68,293 -> 67,525 Mi exactly as modelled, nothing Pending.

### DEFERRED — on-demand (item 2), and why

Survey done: **26 live pods hold 20.7 Gi while burning <10 millicores each.** Most are idle *by nature* (keycloak, litellm, apisix, grafana, nessie, bifrost) - low CPU because they wait for requests; parking them breaks SSO and the gateway on first use. Network traffic, not CPU, was the discriminating signal.

Best candidates: the standalone `opensearch` **namespace (2.5 Gi reserved, 0.74 KiB/s traffic)** - its own manifest calls it a *"search/log playground (standalone; NOT used by DataHub)"* - plus **n8n** (0.31 Gi, and U14 says it has no assigned purpose). Tier B: kokoro, mlflow, neo4j.

**Deferred deliberately.** \~2.8 Gi is \~4% of the node, and there is **no robust on-demand workload manager** - which is not an oversight but the consequence of a decision already recorded at `k8s/argocd/applications/helm-apps.yaml:267-275`: ceding `/spec/replicas` to an external actor was rejected on MECHANISM (a sleeping store reports Synced/Healthy, the accidental-scale-to-zero safety net disappears, sleep state lives only in the cluster). KEDA was retired for the same reason. Parking things today means committing `replicas: 0` to git, one service at a time. **Re-open when a workload manager exists that does not require that carve-out.**

### Measurement traps hit while doing this (all three produced wrong answers first)

1. **cAdvisor emits several series per container.** Summing them tripled Trino to 20.9 Gi. Caught because a pod showed 95 Gi on a 72 Gi node. Use `max by (namespace,pod,container)` before summing.
2. **Sum-of-percentiles is not a percentile-of-sum.** Per-pod p95 summed to 121.9 Gi against a 67.4 Gi real peak. Correctly computed, meaningless.
3. **7-day windows include DEAD pods.** The first on-demand survey listed seven `dagster-user-code-*` ReplicaSets and claimed "55 idle pods holding 47.0 Gi"; intersecting with running pods gave 26 pods / 20.7 Gi. This is the memory version of the terminal-pod trap already recorded below for CPU.

### Still open

**Item 3 - the alert.** Both failures that motivated this issue were silent (a 40-minute Pending scan; a missed postgres backup surfacing only as an Argo badge). A Pending-duration alert is cheap and independent of the workload-manager question.

---

mother's CPU **requests** are over-committed while the node sits nearly idle. This is a scheduling wall, not a capacity problem, and it has already caused two real outages.

## Measured 2026-08-20

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Node allocatable | **16 cores** |
| Requested by scheduled pods | **\~17.1 cores** — over the ceiling |
| Actual node CPU usage | **\~19%** (\~3 cores) |
| Busiest pod in the entire cluster | **0.12 cores** (cassandra-0) |
| Top 10 pods by usage, combined | **\~0.58 cores** |

Roughly **14 cores of reservation are fiction**. The scheduler refuses new pods while \~80% of the CPU sits idle.

## What it actually broke

1. `code-scan-suite` **sat Pending for 40+ minutes** — `FailedScheduling: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu`, no preemption victims. It asks for only 250m. No request size would have helped: the node was already past its ceiling before the scan asked for anything.
2. A postgres backup was missed. `postgres-backup` CronJob: `lastScheduleTime 2026-08-20T03:30Z` but `lastSuccessfulTime 2026-08-19T03:42Z`. The pod almost certainly could not schedule at 03:30 and died on `activeDeadlineSeconds`. This surfaced only as an Argo "Degraded" badge that looked cosmetic — **a silently missed database backup presenting as a UI annoyance.**

Both were diagnosed the long way round. Neither had an alert.

## Not a new problem

`k8s/data-mesh/flink-session.yaml` already carries the comment *"node CPU-requests are saturated; JM is coordination-only, runs fine throttled (lab)"* — the JobManager was trimmed to 0.25 for exactly this reason. Same class as the `istiod-request-node-wall` memory (memory-requests wall from istiod over-reservation). We keep treating symptoms one manifest at a time.

## Already done (symptom relief, 2026-08-20)

* `llama-guard`: `cpu: "1"` → `100m` — reserved a full core, uses <0.03, has **no CPU limit** so inference still bursts freely. Frees \~0.9.
* `code-scan-suite`: `250m` → `100m` — batch job, no latency SLO; a large *reservation* buys it nothing.

## The actual work

1. **Fleet-wide right-sizing pass.** Compare `kube_pod_container_resource_requests` against real `container_cpu_usage_seconds_total` per pod and bring reservations near observed p95. \~50 pods; most reserve 0.25 and use \~0.
2. **Move more systems on-demand.** The `store-scaler` / KEDA wake-sleep mechanism already exists for Tier-2 stores — extend the pattern. Candidates seen awake and idle: `ray-head` (up 7d), `promptfoo`, `neodash`, `a2a-inspector`, `kokoro`, Flink taskmanagers. On-demand beats trimming, because a sleeping pod reserves nothing.
3. **Alert before it bites.** A `FailedScheduling`/`Pending`-duration alert routed to Telegram. Both failures today were silent — one was a missed backup. Per the DoD §6 "Triggered" pillar, a thing that must stay fresh needs a freshness signal.
4. **Consider whether requests are the right tool at all** on a single-node $0 lab. They exist for bin-packing across nodes; with one node they mostly manufacture artificial scarcity. A deliberate convention (tiny requests + limits where it matters) may beat per-service tuning.

## Measurement gotcha — worth keeping

`sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests)` **double-counts**: both kube-state-metrics *and* opencost publish that metric. Pin `job="kube-state-metrics"`. A `node=` filter also still includes terminal (Succeeded/Failed) pods that no longer reserve anything. When in doubt, trust the scheduler's own `FailedScheduling` message over a reconstructed sum.

Backlog: B134. Relates B133 (surfaced during its DoD sweep), B130 (backups), the `store-scaler` easy-button work.
